acquiring or issuing identifier identification option is selected, the report Destination Identifier is placed in the Destination

identification option should be selected if the processor wants report records in acquiring or issuing identifier sequence. If
this option is not used, the Report Destination processor is placed in the Destination Identifier field. The processor is always
in the report records for summary-level SREs.

Machine-readable (TC 46) records are organized by VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) report. Each
report line of data has one or two records, depending on the transaction format used. Common
report information appears in the first record for each report line of data. If a second record is
required, the common report information is not included in that record. The transaction format used
for the machine-readable record depends on the report.
Each record begins with a “46” (positions 1 and 2), and all reports belong to Report Group V
(position 59). There are nine (9) different transaction formats, identified by the Report Subgroup
(position 60). All transaction formats consist of one transaction component record (TCR), except for
Report Subgroups 4, 6, and 9, which consist of two TCRs. The TCR is identified in Transaction
Single Message System (SMS)-connected clients using a Direct Access Service (DAS) VisaNet Access
Point (VAP) for report delivery receive the machine-readable records in the file type of SETLM.
SMS-connected clients using non-VAP delivery receive the machine-readable records as a separate
transmission. There is no header or trailer record.
BASE II-connected clients and SMS-connected clients using a BASE II VAP receive the machine-
readable records in their Center Transaction File (CTF)—Incoming Interchange.

SMS reports have four levels of reporting entities.
The four levels of reporting entities are:
The funds transfer SRE is the level at which funds transfer occurs. The funds transfer SRE can be at any level in the VSS hierarchy.
A processor is a Visa endpoint (or Visa-approved third-party) that provides authorization, clearing, or settlement services for merchants and
clients. The processor captures transactions counts and amounts online. A running total of counts and amounts is accumulated every 30
minutes. The system stores these totals as advice messages (0520) for recovery by the processor.
The affiliate ID can be an issuer, an acquirer, or both. Transactions for all card ranges assigned to an affiliate ID appear on the affiliate IDs
SMS reports generate a total and force a page-break any time a reporting level changes. So, if a client has an affiliate ID associated
with multiple SREs or processors, it may be necessary to add the subtotals to obtain the total activity for an affiliate.
